   446	    /// Attach a Transport to this session. Moves the inner boxed trait
   447	    /// object out of the `transport` wrapper (consuming it from JS's
   448	    /// perspective — subsequent calls fail).
   449	    ///
   450	    /// Mirrors `CollabSession::attach_transport_boxed` on the Rust side
   451	    /// which delegates to the V2 V3 step 1 baseline-reset path: the
   452	    /// next flush sends from empty VV (i.e., ALL local ops including
   453	    /// any appended while no transport was attached — Loro's CRDT op
   454	    /// log IS the implicit offline queue).
   455	    ///
   456	    /// V2.1 does NOT return the prior transport (if any) to JS. The
   457	    /// Rust side drops the returned `Box` immediately. Rationale: the
   458	    /// IDE has no use for the opaque prior transport, and exposing it
   459	    /// would require either creating another `Transport` wrapper
   460	    /// (defeating "this transport is now invalid" semantics) or a
   461	    /// special-cased "detached prior" type. V2.3+ may revisit if a use
   462	    /// case emerges.
   463	    ///
   464	    /// **Failure modes**:
   465	    /// - `transport` has already been used (its `inner` is `None`) →
   466	    ///   JS Error "Transport has already been consumed".
   467	    #[napi(js_name = "attachTransport")]
   468	    pub fn attach_transport(&self, transport: &mut Transport) -> Result<()> {
   469	        let boxed = transport.take_inner().ok_or_else(|| {
   470	            // V2.1 audit closure (Codex LOW-1, 2026-05-22): error wording
   471	            // standardized. A "spent LoopbackPair" throws at takeA/takeB
   472	            // BEFORE producing a Transport — so a consumed Transport
   473	            // wrapper must have come from attachTransport (or a future
   474	            // consumer added in V2.3+).
   475	            Error::from_reason("Transport has already been consumed by attachTransport".to_string())
   476	        })?;
   477	        // attach_transport_boxed handles baseline-reset + replacement.
   478	        // The Option<Box> it returns is the PRIOR transport; we drop
   479	        // it here intentionally (see method docstring).
   480	        let mut inner = self.inner.lock();
   481	        let _prior = inner.attach_transport_boxed(boxed);
   482	        Ok(())
   483	    }

   739	    // ==========================================================
   740	    //
   741	    // **V2.4 closure of V2.3 audit (2026-05-22)**: V2.3 shipped
   742	    // `flushPendingToTransport` as `pub async unsafe fn(&mut self)`,
   743	    // then REMOVED it in the V2.3 closure after Codex FAIL + Opus
   744	    // PASS-WITH-FINDINGS converged on 2 HIGH (Rust UB via napi
   745	    // `&mut self` async re-entry + tokio runtime starvation).
   746	    //
   747	    // V2.4 reintroduces via **Option (a) from V2.3's closure plan**:
   748	    // engine refactor to `Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<CoreCollabSession>>`.
   749	    // This refactor (above) converted ALL CollabSession napi methods
   750	    // from `&mut self` to `&self` with internal `inner.lock()`. The
   751	    // napi-rs codegen now produces `&'static CollabSession` (immutable
   752	    // shared) instead of `&'static mut CollabSession` — no aliasing
   753	    // hazard at all, since multiple `&` to the same instance are
   754	    // sound by Rust's rules.
   755	    //
   756	    // For the async method specifically:

   758	    //     `unsafe`, AND no aliasing UB possible.
   759	    //   - `Arc::clone(&self.inner)` → spawn_blocking → `lock()` inside
   760	    //     the blocking task. The Condvar wait runs on a dedicated
   761	    //     blocking thread (NOT a tokio worker), closing V2.3 HIGH-2.
   762	    //   - The `Arc + Mutex` composition is `Send + Sync` (Mutex<T>:
   763	    //     Send + Sync when T: Send), so the clone-and-move into
   764	    //     spawn_blocking is sound.
   765	
   766	    /// Async flush-pending — waits for the attached transport's writer
   767	    /// task to drain (level-1 local ack per V2 V4 V1 Tier K1 contract).
   768	    ///
   769	    /// Returns a JS `Promise<void>` that resolves when:
   770	    /// - the writer has completed `send` for every queued blob, OR
   771	    /// - the transport has been detached / dropped / errored.
   772	    ///
   773	    /// **V2.4 soundness** (closes V2.3 audit Codex+Opus HIGH-1+HIGH-2):
   774	    ///
   775	    /// - Takes `&self` (not `&mut self`). napi-rs codegen produces
   776	    ///   `&'static CollabSession` → multiple aliasing reads are sound
   777	    ///   by Rust's rules. No UB even under JS re-entry.
   778	    /// - `Arc::clone(&self.inner)` extracts a cloned reference to the
   779	    ///   inner `Arc<Mutex<CoreCollabSession>>`. The clone is moved into
   780	    ///   `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`, which runs on a dedicated
   781	    ///   blocking thread (NOT a tokio worker). The Condvar wait
   782	    ///   doesn't occupy the napi-rs runtime's worker pool — closes
   783	    ///   V2.3 HIGH-2 (runtime starvation).
   784	    /// - Inside the blocking task, `inner.lock()` acquires the mutex.
   785	    ///   If a concurrent JS call holds the lock (e.g., another
   786	    ///   mid-flight method), this call blocks until the lock is
   787	    ///   available. No deadlock because mutex order is consistent
   788	    ///   (all session methods acquire the SAME mutex).
   789	    ///
   790	    /// **Failure modes**:
   791	    /// - No transport attached → returns `Ok(())` (NOT a rejection).
   792	    /// - Transport error during the wait → JS Error.
   793	    /// - The `spawn_blocking` task panics → JS Error.
   794	    #[napi(js_name = "flushPendingToTransport")]
   795	    pub async fn flush_pending_to_transport(&self) -> Result<()> {
   796	        let inner = Arc::clone(&self.inner);
   797	        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
   798	            let mut guard = inner.lock();
   799	            guard.flush_pending_to_transport()
   800	        })
   801	        .await
   802	        .map_err(|e| Error::from_reason(format!("flushPendingToTransport task: {e}")))?
   803	        .map_err(|e| Error::from_reason(format!("{e}")))
   804	    }
   805	}

   848	            env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),

   913	    /// - `WebSocketError::ConnectFailed` — TCP/DNS error.
   914	    /// - `WebSocketError::HandshakeFailed` — WS upgrade rejected
   915	    ///   (e.g., HTTP 401, protocol mismatch).

   919	    /// (reader + writer). On detach, the tasks are aborted via the
   920	    /// engine's `WebSocketTransport::Drop`. Don't hold the Transport

   927	    /// completes — no manual ThreadsafeFunction plumbing needed.

   975	/// `Vec<Transport>` fails the trait bound `ObjectFinalize` napi-rs

   416	    /// peer to open a collaborative workbook).

   418	    /// `bytes` is a `LoroDoc::export(ExportMode::Snapshot)` produced

   751	    /// direct Rust callers and now delegates to this method to keep
   752	    /// the baseline-reset + replacement semantics in one place.
   753	    ///

   756	    /// `Option<Box<dyn Transport + Send>>` owns the prior transport's

   758	    /// tasks + TCP socket); silent drops leak the socket. The matching

   760	    /// Opus-B LOW-3 (asymmetry between attach + detach).

   762	                  holding it past attach keeps the old TCP socket alive"]
   763	    pub fn attach_transport_boxed(
   764	        &mut self,
   765	        transport: Box<dyn Transport + Send>,
   766	    ) -> Option<Box<dyn Transport + Send>> {
   767	        // **V2 V3 step 1 contract**: every attach resets the VV baseline
   768	        // so the next flush sends from empty. A new transport-peer hasn't
   769	        // seen ANY of this session's ops; without this reset they'd miss
   770	        // ops 0..stale_vv and end up with a corrupt view. This is the
   771	        // authoritative site for the invariant — `attach_transport<T>`
   772	        // delegates here (V2.1 refactor).

   777	    /// **Phase 5.5 V2 V1 (2026-05-19):** detach the current
   778	    /// transport. Returns it for caller cleanup; returns `None`
   779	    /// if no transport was attached.

   784	    /// to release them — holding it past the reconnect handshake

    56	/// Create a custom Tokio runtime used by the NAPI-RS.
    57	/// You can control the tokio runtime configuration by yourself.
    58	/// ### Example
    59	/// ```no_run
    60	/// use tokio::runtime::Builder;
    61	/// use napi::create_custom_tokio_runtime;
    62	///
    63	/// #[napi_derive::module_init]
    64	/// fn init() {
    65	///    let rt = Builder::new_multi_thread().enable_all().thread_stack_size(32 * 1024 * 1024).build().unwrap();
    66	///    create_custom_tokio_runtime(rt);
    67	/// }
    68	pub fn create_custom_tokio_runtime(rt: Runtime) {
    69	  USER_DEFINED_RT.get_or_init(move || RwLock::new(Some(rt)));
    70	  IS_USER_DEFINED_RT.get_or_init(|| true);
    71	}

    77	/// Start the async runtime (Currently is tokio).
    78	///
    79	/// In Node.js native targets the async runtime will be dropped when Node env exits.
    80	/// But in Electron renderer process, the Node env will exits and recreate when the window reloads.
    81	/// So we need to ensure that the async runtime is initialized when the Node env is created.
    82	///
    83	/// In wasm targets, the async runtime will not been shutdown automatically due to the limitation of the wasm runtime.
    84	/// So, you need to call `shutdown_async_runtime` function to manually shutdown the async runtime.
    85	/// In some scenarios, you may want to start the async runtime again like in tests.
    86	pub fn start_async_runtime() {
    87	  if let Ok(mut rt) = RT.write() {
    88	    if rt.is_none() {
    89	      *rt = Some(create_runtime());
    90	    }
    91	  }
    92	}

   154	pub fn within_runtime_if_available<F: FnOnce() -> T, T>(f: F) -> T {

   164	    })

   468	    /// These threads are used for blocking operations like tasks spawned

   480	    ///
   481	    /// The default value is 512.
   482	    ///
   483	    /// # Queue Behavior
   484	    ///
   485	    /// When a blocking task is submitted, it will be inserted into a queue. If available, one of
   486	    /// the idle threads will be notified to run the task. Otherwise, if the threshold set by this
   487	    /// method has not been reached, a new thread will be spawned. If no idle thread is available

     2	//!
     3	//! **Phase 5.2.a (2026-05-19, scaffold):** trait shape defined.

     7	//! `CollabSession` exposes 5 typed transport methods
     8	//! (`attach_transport` / `detach_transport` / `has_transport` /

    10	//! V2 V1 is "explicit drive" — caller invokes flush + poll on a

    12	//! **Phase 5.5 V2 V2 (2026-05-21):** `AutoFlushPolicy` enum on
    13	//! `CollabSession`. Opt-in `OnAppend` invokes flush automatically
    14	//! after every mutator. Default is `Disabled` (V2 V1 behavior
    15	//! preserved). See [`crate::AutoFlushPolicy`] +
    16	//! [`crate::CollabSession::set_auto_flush_policy`].
    17	//! **Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 1 (2026-05-21):** version-vector tracking
    18	//! for the **currently attached** transport baseline + delta flushes.
    19	//! `CollabSession::flush_delta_to_transport` sends only the delta
    20	//! since the last successful flush via `LoroDoc::ExportMode::Updates`.
    21	//! Auto-flush routes through this delta path — wire payload is
    22	//! O(per-op delta) instead of O(full state). Idempotency
    23	//! short-circuit (no state change → no send) closes the V2 V2
    24	//! echo-loop concern. The checkpoint is
    25	//! per-session-currently-attached-transport, NOT per-transport-
    26	//! identity (`attach_transport` resets the baseline).
    27	//! **Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 2 (2026-05-21):** wires `poll_remote*`
    28	//! into auto-flush. After a successful drain (`merged > 0`), one
    29	//! auto-flush fires per call (not per-blob — bandwidth-efficient).
    30	//! V2 V3 step 1's idempotency guard prevents echo loops: drained
    31	//! bytes that Loro dedupes leave the VV unchanged → flush
    32	//! short-circuits to `Ok(false)`. 3-peer hub-fanout pattern now
    33	//! works automatically under `OnAppend`.
    34	//! **Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 3 (2026-05-21):** offline-write story.
    35	//! Investigation showed no explicit queue is needed: Loro's CRDT op
    36	//! log IS the implicit offline queue. Append while no transport
    37	//! attached → `maybe_auto_flush` no-ops; op committed locally. On
    38	//! reattach: `attach_transport` resets `last_flushed_vv = None`; the
    39	//! next mutator (or explicit `flush_delta_to_transport`) sends from
    40	//! empty VV — delivers ALL accumulated ops including offline ones.
    41	//! Adds `has_pending_flush() -> bool` ergonomic helper (compares
    42	//! current VV vs last-flushed VV). 7 new integration tests pin the
    43	//! offline-write contract.

    45	//! **Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 4 (2026-05-21, this ship):** first
    46	//! production-grade `Transport` impl ships as a separate crate,

   100	use thiserror::Error;
   101	
   102	/// Errors emitted by `Transport` impls.
   103	#[derive(Debug, Error)]
   104	#[non_exhaustive]
   105	pub enum TransportError {
   106	    /// The underlying I/O failed (socket dead, network partition,
   107	    /// etc.). Implementations should distinguish recoverable
   108	    /// (reconnect) from permanent (auth rejected) failures via
   109	    /// variant structure in their own error type, then map to this
   110	    /// variant at the trait boundary if they don't want to expose
   111	    /// implementation details.
   112	    #[error("transport I/O error: {0}")]
   113	    Io(String),
   114	
   115	    /// The transport is closed and no further sends are accepted.
   116	    /// Receivers should still drain any already-queued bytes via
   117	    /// `try_recv` before considering the channel done.
   118	    #[error("transport closed")]
   119	    Closed,
   120	}
   121	
   122	/// Wire-byte channel for Phase 5 collaboration.
   123	///
   124	/// Implementations push and pull opaque byte blobs. The blobs ARE
   125	/// Loro `LoroDoc::export(...)` snapshots / updates; the
   126	/// transport doesn't interpret them. Framing (where one blob ends
   127	/// and the next starts) is the implementation's responsibility.
   128	pub trait Transport {
   129	    /// Push `bytes` to the channel. Implementations may buffer
   130	    /// internally; the call returns when the bytes are
   131	    /// **queued for send**, not when the remote has received them.
   132	    ///
   133	    /// **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Codex M1 + Opus-B M1,
   134	    /// 2026-05-21):** for buffered impls (`WebSocketTransport` and
   135	    /// future async transports), there is a window between "send
   136	    /// returned Ok" and "bytes on the wire" where the bytes can be
   137	    /// silently lost (transport dropped, peer disconnect mid-flush,
   138	    /// allocator failure during the writer task). The session's
   139	    /// [`crate::CollabSession::flush_delta_to_transport`] advances
   140	    /// `last_flushed_vv` immediately on `send`'s Ok return, so
   141	    /// `has_pending_flush() == false` alone means "queued to the
   142	    /// currently-attached transport," NOT "the peer has received the
   143	    /// ops." **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (2026-05-21) Tier K1 closure**: call
   144	    /// [`Transport::flush_pending`] after `flush_delta_to_transport`
   145	    /// to block until the writer task has completed `ws_sink.send`
   146	    /// for every queued blob — that provides level-1 (local writer)
   147	    /// ack. For stronger guarantees (peer-application ack, TCP-level
   148	    /// ack), keep the transport attached until you've verified peer
   149	    /// reception out-of-band (e.g., via a custom ack-op layered on
   150	    /// `merge_bytes`). On transport drop or `Err(Closed)`, detach +
   151	    /// reattach a new transport — the V2 V3 step 1 baseline-reset
   152	    /// contract re-sends from empty VV.
   153	    ///
   154	    /// On error, the caller should treat the byte blob as unsent
   155	    /// and re-queue (or surface the error to the user). The
   156	    /// transport will not retry automatically — that policy lives
   157	    /// at the layer above (Phase 5.5 design will pick reconnect
   158	    /// semantics).
   159	    fn send(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), TransportError>;
   160	
   161	    /// Non-blocking receive. Returns `Some(bytes)` if a blob is
   162	    /// queued, `None` otherwise. Implementations choose how often
   163	    /// they poll the underlying channel; the contract is "if you
   164	    /// have something, give it to me, else `None`."
   165	    ///
   166	    /// Returns `Err(TransportError::Closed)` only when the channel
   167	    /// is permanently closed AND its internal queue is empty. A
   168	    /// transient I/O failure during poll surfaces as
   169	    /// `Err(TransportError::Io)`.
   170	    fn try_recv(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, TransportError>;
   171	
   172	    /// Read the most recent transport-internal error, if any. Default
   173	    /// returns `None` for impls without a runtime-error concept
   174	    /// (`NoopTransport`, `LoopbackTransport`). Buffered async impls
   175	    /// (`WebSocketTransport`) override to expose the underlying cause
   176	    /// of the most recent task-observed failure.
   177	    ///
   178	    /// **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Opus-A H1, 2026-05-21):** the
   179	    /// V2 V3 step 4 closure added `WebSocketTransport::last_error()`
   180	    /// on the concrete type for IDE consumers driving reconnect

   182	    /// concrete type into `Box<dyn Transport + Send>`, making it
   183	    /// unreachable. Lifting the accessor to the trait + adding
   184	    /// [`crate::CollabSession::transport_last_error`] proxy is the
   185	    /// minimum-viable fix: IDE callers can now distinguish "peer
   186	    /// reset" from "auth rejected" from "capacity exceeded" without
   187	    /// downcasting or holding a parallel handle.
   188	    ///

   190	    /// error type to keep the trait minimal and avoid leaking
   191	    /// impl-specific types (`WebSocketError`, etc.). Consumers
   192	    /// pattern-match on substring or just display the message.
   193	    ///
   194	    /// Read AFTER observing [`TransportError::Closed`] from `send`
   195	    /// or `try_recv`. Returns `None` for clean shutdowns (caller
   196	    /// `close()`, graceful peer Close frame, transport never failed).
   197	    fn last_error(&self) -> Option<String> {
   198	        None
   199	    }

   201	    /// Block until every byte blob previously queued via `send` has
   202	    /// been written to the underlying transport's wire (e.g. WebSocket
   203	    /// sink). Default `Ok(())` for synchronous transports
   204	    /// (`LoopbackTransport`, `NoopTransport`) where `send` is already
   205	    /// wire-delivery — there is no buffer to drain.
   206	    ///
   207	    /// **Phase 5.5 V2 V4 V1 step 1 (2026-05-21) — Tier K1 ack channel.**
   208	    /// Closes the V2 V3 step 5 megaudit's convergent finding (Codex M1
   209	    /// and Opus-B M1): buffered async transports
   210	    /// (`WebSocketTransport`) return `Ok` from `send` once bytes are
   211	    /// queued in an mpsc channel, NOT when bytes reach the wire.

   214	    /// not "delivered." For IDE consumers building "safe to close

   216	    /// lets callers block until the local writer has caught up,
   217	    /// providing a level-1 ack (bytes hit `ws_sink.send`
   218	    /// successfully). TCP-ack (level 2) and peer-application-ack
   219	    /// (level 3) require lower-layer hooks or custom protocols
   220	    /// respectively.
   220	    /// respectively.
   221	    ///
   222	    /// # Errors
   223	    ///
   224	    /// - `Err(TransportError::Closed)` if the transport is closed
   225	    ///   (either before `flush_pending` was called OR during the wait
   226	    ///   — e.g., writer task failed mid-flush and set the closed
   227	    ///   flag).
   228	    /// - `Err(TransportError::Io)` for internal synchronization
   229	    ///   failures (mutex poisoning from a panicked task).

   231	    /// # Async-context caveat

   233	    /// `flush_pending` is blocking-sync (uses `Condvar::wait_timeout`).
   234	    /// Calling it from within a tokio task body will block the
   235	    /// runtime worker. Wrap with `tokio::task::block_in_place` (on

   237	    /// any runtime) to avoid stalling other tasks.
   238	    fn flush_pending(&mut self) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
   239	        Ok(())

   243	/// No-op `Transport` impl for tests + scaffolding.
   244	///
   245	/// Records every `send` call in an internal `Vec` (so tests can
   246	/// assert what would have gone over the wire) and `try_recv`

   250	/// [`LoopbackTransport::pair`] instead — `NoopTransport` is for

   255	    /// inspect this to verify their `CollabSession` calls emit the

   293	/// **Phase 5.5 V1 (2026-05-19):** in-process paired `Transport`
   294	/// impl for 2-peer round-trip testing.
   295	///
   296	/// Constructed via [`LoopbackTransport::pair`]: returns two
   297	/// endpoints `(a, b)` where `a.send(bytes)` lands in `b`'s recv
   298	/// queue and vice versa. The two endpoints share two
   299	/// `Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<Vec<u8>>>>` channels via interior
   300	/// mutability — `Send + Sync` so they can also be used across
   301	/// threads if a future test wants that.
   302	///
   303	/// ## Use case
   304	///
   305	/// Wire two `CollabSession`s together for tests like:
   306	/// ```ignore
   307	/// let (mut tx_a, mut tx_b) = LoopbackTransport::pair();
   308	/// let session_a = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(1))?;
   309	/// let session_b = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(2))?;
   310	/// // ... append ops on a, drain via tx_a.send / tx_b.try_recv ...
   311	/// ```
   312	///
   313	/// **Phase 5.5 V2 V2 (2026-05-21):** `CollabSession` supports
   314	/// opt-in auto-flush via `AutoFlushPolicy::OnAppend` — every
   315	/// session mutator (`append_op`, `merge_bytes`, presence writes,
   316	/// `undo` / `redo` when consumed, `sweep_presence`) then sends
   317	/// through the attached transport automatically. Default policy
   318	/// remains `Disabled` (V2 V1 explicit-drive behavior). Tests can
   319	/// still drive the flow manually: append, export_bytes, send via
   320	/// the transport, recv on the other side, merge_bytes — useful
   321	/// when the test wants deterministic control over when bytes
   322	/// land on the wire (e.g. ordering tests). **Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 2
   323	/// (2026-05-21):** `poll_remote*` now also triggers auto-flush after
   324	/// a non-empty drain (one flush per call, not per-blob). See
   325	/// [`crate::AutoFlushPolicy::OnAppend`] for the receive-side
   326	/// contract.
   327	///
   328	/// ## Close semantics
   329	///
   330	/// Each endpoint has its OWN `closed` flag (separate
   331	/// `AtomicBool`). `a.close()` shuts down endpoint A:
   332	/// - A's `send` returns `TransportError::Closed` immediately.
   333	/// - A's `try_recv` drains any already-queued bytes FIRST and
   334	///   only returns `Closed` once the queue is empty (per the
   335	///   `Transport` trait contract at the trait docstring).
   336	/// - B is unaffected: B can still `send` (bytes land in A's
   337	///   inbox; A drains them on the next try_recv before reporting
   338	///   Closed) and `try_recv` (drains B's inbox).
   339	///
   340	/// ## Atomic ordering caveat
   341	///
   342	/// `close` uses `AtomicBool` with `Relaxed` ordering. For
   343	/// cross-thread "close then send" semantics, callers must use
   344	/// external synchronization — a thread that observes
   345	/// `is_closed() == true` after another thread's `close()` is NOT
   346	/// guaranteed by this transport alone (the atomic only protects
   347	/// the flag itself, not the surrounding sequence).
   348	pub struct LoopbackTransport {
   349	    /// Channel WE drain via `try_recv`. The peer's `send` writes
   350	    /// here.
   351	    inbox: Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<Vec<u8>>>>,
   352	    /// Channel WE write to via `send`. The peer's `try_recv`
   353	    /// drains here.
   354	    outbox: Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<Vec<u8>>>>,
   355	    /// Per-endpoint close flag. Atomic so `close(&self)` doesn't
   356	    /// need `&mut`.
   357	    closed: AtomicBool,
   358	}
   359	
   360	impl std::fmt::Debug for LoopbackTransport {
   360	impl std::fmt::Debug for LoopbackTransport {
   361	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
   362	        f.debug_struct("LoopbackTransport")
   363	            .field(
   364	                "inbox_len",
   365	                &self.inbox.lock().map(|q| q.len()).unwrap_or(0),
   366	            )
   367	            .field(
   368	                "outbox_len",
   369	                &self.outbox.lock().map(|q| q.len()).unwrap_or(0),
   370	            )
   371	            .field("closed", &self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
   372	            .finish()
   373	    }
   374	}
   375	
   376	impl LoopbackTransport {
   377	    /// Construct a pair of `LoopbackTransport` endpoints. Returns
   378	    /// `(a, b)` where `a.send(...)` enqueues to `b.try_recv()` and
   379	    /// `b.send(...)` enqueues to `a.try_recv()`.
   380	    pub fn pair() -> (Self, Self) {
   381	        let a_to_b = Arc::new(Mutex::new(VecDeque::new()));
   382	        let b_to_a = Arc::new(Mutex::new(VecDeque::new()));
   383	        let a = Self {
   384	            inbox: b_to_a.clone(),
   385	            outbox: a_to_b.clone(),
   386	            closed: AtomicBool::new(false),
   387	        };
   388	        let b = Self {
   389	            inbox: a_to_b,
   390	            outbox: b_to_a,
   391	            closed: AtomicBool::new(false),
   392	        };
   393	        (a, b)
   394	    }
   395	
   396	    /// Mark this endpoint closed. Subsequent `send` / `try_recv`
   397	    /// calls return `TransportError::Closed`. The peer endpoint
   398	    /// is NOT affected by this call (each side has its own close
   399	    /// flag).
   400	    pub fn close(&self) {
   401	        self.closed.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   402	    }
   403	
   404	    /// True if this endpoint has been closed.
   405	    pub fn is_closed(&self) -> bool {
   406	        self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
   407	    }
   408	
   409	    /// Number of bytes blobs waiting in this endpoint's inbox
   410	    /// (i.e. sent by the peer, not yet drained via `try_recv`).
   411	    /// Useful for tests that want to assert "the peer sent N
   412	    /// blobs to me" without consuming them.
   413	    pub fn pending_recv(&self) -> usize {
   414	        self.inbox.lock().map(|q| q.len()).unwrap_or(0)
   415	    }
   416	}
   417	
   418	impl Transport for LoopbackTransport {
   419	    fn send(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
   420	        if self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
   421	            return Err(TransportError::Closed);
   422	        }
   423	        self.outbox
   424	            .lock()
   425	            .map_err(|e| TransportError::Io(format!("loopback outbox lock poisoned: {e}")))?
   426	            .push_back(bytes.to_vec());
   427	        Ok(())
   428	    }
   429	
   430	    fn try_recv(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, TransportError> {
   431	        // Trait contract (transport.rs:71-74): "Closed only when the
   432	        // channel is permanently closed AND its internal queue is
   433	        // empty." So drain any already-queued bytes first; only
   434	        // return Closed when both closed AND drained.
   435	        // Codex + Opus 5.5 V1 audit MEDIUM/HIGH closure: pre-closure
   436	        // we returned Closed immediately on close, violating the
   437	        // contract.
   438	        let mut queue = self
   439	            .inbox
   440	            .lock()
   441	            .map_err(|e| TransportError::Io(format!("loopback inbox lock poisoned: {e}")))?;
   442	        if let Some(bytes) = queue.pop_front() {
   443	            return Ok(Some(bytes));
   444	        }
   445	        // Queue empty — now distinguish "open but empty" from "closed".
   446	        if self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
   447	            Err(TransportError::Closed)
   448	        } else {
   449	            Ok(None)
   450	        }
   451	    }
   452	}

   457	const _ASSERT_LOOPBACK_TRANSPORT_SEND_SYNC: fn() = || {
   458	    fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}
   459	    assert_send_sync::<LoopbackTransport>();
   460	};

     1	//! `ql-collab-ws` — WebSocket `Transport` impl for Phase 5
     2	//! collaboration.
     3	//!
     4	//! **Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 4 (2026-05-21, this ship):** first
     5	//! production-grade [`Transport`](ql_collab::Transport) impl. Bridges
     6	//! tokio-tungstenite's async WebSocket client to the sync `Transport`
     7	//! trait via `tokio::sync::mpsc` channels and two spawned background
     8	//! tasks.
     9	//!
    10	//! ## Crate boundary rationale
    11	//!
    12	//! `ql-collab` core is purely sync and embeddable in non-tokio
    13	//! runtimes (e.g., an IDE main thread, future WASM target). Pulling
    14	//! tokio + tokio-tungstenite into the core would force that
    15	//! constraint on every consumer. Keeping the WebSocket impl in a
    16	//! separate crate means:
    17	//! - Consumers who only need `LoopbackTransport` (tests) or a custom
    18	//!   transport (in-process IPC, gRPC streaming) don't pay for tokio.
    19	//! - The async runtime lives at the application boundary, not in the
    20	//!   collaboration layer.
    21	//!
    22	//! ## Architecture
    23	//!
    24	//! ```text
    25	//!  caller (sync, e.g. inside CollabSession::append_op)
    26	//!    │
    27	//!    │  send(bytes)        try_recv() -> Option<bytes>
    28	//!    ▼                            ▲
    29	//!  WebSocketTransport             │
    30	//!    │ outbound_tx              inbound_rx
    31	//!    │  (mpsc::UnboundedSender)  (mpsc::UnboundedReceiver)
    32	//!    ▼                            ▲
    33	//!  writer_task (tokio)          reader_task (tokio)
    34	//!    │  awaits outbound_rx        │  awaits ws_stream.next()
    35	//!    ▼                            ▲
    36	//!    │  ws_sink.send(Binary)      │  inbound_tx.send(bytes)
    37	//!    ▼                            │
    38	//!  ===================== TCP socket =====================
    39	//! ```
    40	//!
    41	//! The two background tasks own the WebSocket halves
    42	//! (`SplitSink` + `SplitStream` via `futures_util::StreamExt::split`).
    43	//! `Drop` aborts both tasks (RAII close).
    44	//!
    45	//! ## V1 limitations (deferred to V2 V4)
    46	//!
    47	//! - **No TLS (`ws://` only).** Use a TLS-terminating reverse proxy
    48	//!   in front, or wait for V2 V4 `rustls` feature.
    49	//! - **No auto-reconnect.** Caller drives via `detach_transport` +
    50	//!   new `connect` + `attach_transport`. The Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 1
    51	//!   `last_flushed_vv = None` reset on attach delivers all accumulated
    52	//!   ops on reconnect (offline-write story).
    53	//! - **Unbounded outbound mpsc queue.** Memory growth is bounded in
    54	//!   practice for the common disconnect case: when the peer closes
    55	//!   the TCP socket, the reader task observes EOF / `Err` and sets
    56	//!   the closed flag; subsequent `send` calls fast-path to
    57	//!   `Err(Closed)` before reaching the unbounded mpsc. The genuine
    58	//!   growth window is the **dead-peer-but-not-closed** scenario
    59	//!   (server stops draining but doesn't tear down the TCP socket):
    60	//!   `ws_sink.send` stalls on TCP backpressure, `outbound_rx` grows
    61	//!   unboundedly, and the reader task may still be receiving heartbeat
    62	//!   frames so `closed` stays false. V2 V4 will switch to bounded
    63	//!   with caller-configurable backpressure policy (clarified in
    64	//!   V2 V3 step 4 audit closure, Opus M5).
    65	//! - **Client-only.** Server-side WebSocket impls use other libraries
    66	//!   (`axum-tungstenite`, `warp::ws`, etc.).
    67	//! - **Drops text/ping/pong/close frames as inbound data.** Loro
    68	//!   payloads are binary blobs; non-binary frames don't carry our
    69	//!   protocol. Close frames trigger reader task exit. Inbound Ping
    70	//!   frames: tokio-tungstenite queues a Pong response on the sink
    71	//!   for the next write — but with no app traffic the Pong is not
    72	//!   flushed until the next app send (clarified in V2 V3 step 4
    73	//!   audit closure, Opus L3). Server-side idle-timeout would then
    74	//!   close the connection. Text frames are silently dropped (a
    75	//!   future protocol extension could add a callback hook).
    76	//!
    77	//! ## Example
    78	//!
    79	//! ```ignore
    80	//! use ql_collab::{CollabSession, PeerId, AutoFlushPolicy};
    81	//! use ql_collab_ws::WebSocketTransport;
    82	//!
    83	//! let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()?;
    84	//! let ws = rt.block_on(WebSocketTransport::connect("ws://localhost:8080"))?;
    85	//! let mut session = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(1))?;
    86	//! session.attach_transport(ws);
    87	//! session.set_auto_flush_policy(AutoFlushPolicy::OnAppend);
    88	//! // ... appends now propagate via WebSocket automatically ...
    89	//! ```
    90	
    91	use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, Ordering};
    92	use std::sync::{Arc, Condvar, Mutex};
    93	use std::time::Duration;
    94	
    95	use futures_util::{SinkExt, StreamExt};
    96	use ql_collab::{Transport, TransportError};
    97	use thiserror::Error;
    98	use tokio::sync::mpsc;
    99	use tokio::task::JoinHandle;
   100	use tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::Message;
   101	
   102	/// **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Opus-B M2, 2026-05-21):**
   103	/// panic-safe task-exit guard. Held by the writer/reader tasks; its
   104	/// `Drop` impl runs even on panic-unwinding. If the task exits
   105	/// without calling [`Self::mark_clean_exit`], the guard treats it as
   106	/// an unexpected exit (panic) and sets `closed = true` + records a
   107	/// `RuntimeError` describing the panic.
   108	///
   109	/// Without this guard, a panic in `ws_sink.send`, `bytes.into()`, or
   110	/// any future inner code would leave the transport in `closed=false`
   111	/// with the task gone — callers would poll `try_recv` forever
   112	/// returning `Ok(None)` and `send` would queue bytes into an
   113	/// orphaned mpsc.
   114	struct TaskExitGuard {
   115	    task_name: &'static str,
   116	    closed: Arc<AtomicBool>,
   117	    last_error: Arc<Mutex<Option<WebSocketError>>>,
   118	    /// **V2 V4 V1 step 1 audit closure (Codex L1 / Opus M2, 2026-05-21):**
   119	    /// notify the `flush_pending` Condvar on panic exit so blocked
   120	    /// callers wake up immediately rather than waiting for the
   121	    /// `wait_timeout` tick. Same Arc as `WebSocketTransport::progress`.
   122	    progress: Arc<(Mutex<u64>, Condvar)>,
   123	    clean: bool,
   124	}
   125	
   126	impl TaskExitGuard {
   127	    fn new(
   128	        task_name: &'static str,
   129	        closed: Arc<AtomicBool>,
   130	        last_error: Arc<Mutex<Option<WebSocketError>>>,
   131	        progress: Arc<(Mutex<u64>, Condvar)>,
   132	    ) -> Self {
   133	        Self {
   134	            task_name,
   135	            closed,
   136	            last_error,
   137	            progress,
   138	            clean: false,
   139	        }
   140	    }
   141	
   142	    /// Call before the task body exits via any normal path
   143	    /// (Err arm, stream-end, clean recv-None). Skipping this
   144	    /// is the signal that the task panicked.
   145	    fn mark_clean_exit(mut self) {
   146	        self.clean = true;
   147	    }
   148	}
   149	
   150	impl Drop for TaskExitGuard {
   151	    fn drop(&mut self) {
   152	        if !self.clean {
   153	            // Panic path: stash the panic signal in last_error
   154	            // BEFORE setting closed (so a concurrent reader sees
   155	            // the error first). Per CLAUDE.md no-fallback rule,
   156	            // surface the panic loudly rather than swallowing.
   157	            record_runtime_error(
   158	                &self.last_error,
   159	                format!("ql-collab-ws {} task panicked", self.task_name),
   160	            );

   163	            // flush_pending waiter so they observe the closed flag

   170	/// **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Opus-B M3, 2026-05-21):** surface
   171	/// poisoned-mutex condition as a `RuntimeError` rather than the
   172	/// previous `.lock().ok()` swallow. A poisoned mutex means a holder
   173	/// panicked while populating the slot — the caller deserves to know
   174	/// the slot's most-recent error was lost.
   175	fn record_runtime_error(slot: &Arc<Mutex<Option<WebSocketError>>>, message: String) {
   176	    match slot.lock() {
   177	        Ok(mut guard) => {
   178	            *guard = Some(WebSocketError::RuntimeError(message));
   179	        }
   180	        Err(poisoned) => {
   181	            // Recover the inner mutex despite poison; overwrite with
   182	            // a message that explicitly notes the poisoning so the
   183	            // caller can detect a prior panic-during-error-stash.
   184	            let mut guard = poisoned.into_inner();
   185	            *guard = Some(WebSocketError::RuntimeError(format!(
   186	                "{message} (note: error slot mutex was poisoned by prior panic)"
   187	            )));
   188	        }
   189	    }
   190	}

   192	/// Errors emitted by [`WebSocketTransport`].
   193	///
   194	/// Distinguishes connect-time errors (`InvalidUrl`, `ConnectFailed`,
   195	/// `HandshakeFailed`) from runtime errors observed by the background
   196	/// reader/writer tasks (`RuntimeError`). Connect-time errors surface
   197	/// as the `Result::Err` from [`WebSocketTransport::connect`]; runtime
   198	/// errors are stashed on the transport and readable via
   199	/// [`WebSocketTransport::last_error`] AFTER the trait `send`/`try_recv`
   200	/// surface `TransportError::Closed`.
   201	///
   202	/// Maps tungstenite errors opaquely — we don't want to leak
   203	/// tungstenite types into the public API.
   204	///
   205	/// **V2 V3 step 4 audit closure (Opus M1, 2026-05-21):** the prior
   206	/// ship discarded background-task errors (`if let Err(_e)`), flattening
   207	/// 8 distinct tungstenite::Error variants into a uniform `Closed` at
   208	/// the trait boundary. This violated the CLAUDE.md no-fallbacks rule
   209	/// (errors must be visible) and made it impossible for IDE consumers
   210	/// driving reconnect handshakes to distinguish "connection lost" from
   211	/// "auth failed". Adds `RuntimeError(String)` variant + `last_error()`
   212	/// accessor; both tasks now populate the shared `last_error` slot on
   213	/// non-graceful exit.
   214	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Error)]
   215	#[non_exhaustive]
   216	pub enum WebSocketError {
   217	    /// The URL string failed to parse or is missing required parts.
   218	    /// Per CLAUDE.md no-fallback rule: surface clearly, don't silently
   219	    /// retry with a "fixed up" URL.
   220	    #[error("invalid WebSocket URL: {0}")]
   221	    InvalidUrl(String),
   222	
   223	    /// TCP connect failed (refused, timeout, DNS, etc.).
   224	    #[error("WebSocket connection failed: {0}")]
   225	    ConnectFailed(String),
   226	
   227	    /// WebSocket protocol handshake failed (HTTP upgrade rejected,
   228	    /// invalid response, etc.).
   229	    #[error("WebSocket handshake failed: {0}")]
   230	    HandshakeFailed(String),
   231	
   232	    /// Background reader/writer task observed a runtime failure
   233	    /// (peer reset, IO error, protocol violation, capacity exceeded,
   234	    /// etc.) AFTER a successful connect. Surfaces via
   235	    /// [`WebSocketTransport::last_error`] once the trait-level
   236	    /// `Closed` has been observed.
   237	    #[error("WebSocket runtime error: {0}")]
   238	    RuntimeError(String),
   239	}

   241	/// Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 4 — WebSocket `Transport` impl.
   242	///
   243	/// Bridges async tokio-tungstenite to the sync `Transport` trait via
   244	/// `tokio::sync::mpsc` channels and two spawned background tasks.
   245	/// See module-level docs for architecture diagram.
   246	///
   247	/// ## Construction
   248	///
   249	/// Use [`connect`](Self::connect) — async fn that performs the WS
   250	/// handshake. Caller pattern from sync code:
   251	///
   252	/// ```ignore
   253	/// let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()?;
   254	/// let ws = rt.block_on(WebSocketTransport::connect("ws://host:port"))?;
   255	/// session.attach_transport(ws);
   256	/// ```
   257	///
   258	/// ## Send + Sync
   259	///
   260	/// `WebSocketTransport: Send + Sync` (Send pinned by the V2 V3
   261	/// step 4 manual `const _ASSERT_WEBSOCKET_TRANSPORT_SEND`, Sync
   262	/// pinned by V2 V4 V1 step 3 `static_assertions::assert_impl_all!` —
   263	/// both compile-time checks at the end of this file). Note: the
   264	/// prior
   265	/// V2 V3 step 4 docstring (and Tier J3 backlog entry) incorrectly
   266	/// claimed `!Sync` based on the intuition that the single-consumer
   267	/// mpsc receiver should prevent sharing. In Rust, `Sync` means "`&T`
   268	/// can be sent across threads" — orthogonal to "`&mut T` access is
   269	/// exclusive." `try_recv` takes `&mut self`, so concurrent receives
   270	/// are already prevented by the borrow checker. All fields
   271	/// (mpsc handles, `Arc<AtomicBool>`, `Arc<Mutex<_>>`, `JoinHandle`)
   272	/// are `Send + Sync`, making the composite `Send + Sync`.
   273	///
   274	/// **Why this matters**: matches the `CollabSession::transport:
   275	/// Box<dyn Transport + Send>` constraint (only `Send` is required at
   276	/// the trait boundary; `Sync` is a bonus that allows future
   277	/// `Arc<WebSocketTransport>` wrappers if a consumer needs them).
   278	/// **Tier J3 closure (V2 V4 V1 step 3, 2026-05-21):** corrected the
   279	/// docstring + the backlog entry; pinned BOTH bounds with positive
   280	/// compile-time asserts.
   281	pub struct WebSocketTransport {
   282	    /// Caller-side sender feeding the writer task. Sync write via
   283	    /// `UnboundedSender::send` (which is non-blocking).
   284	    outbound_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<Vec<u8>>,
   285	    /// Caller-side receiver pulling from the reader task. Sync drain
   286	    /// via `UnboundedReceiver::try_recv`.
   287	    inbound_rx: mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<Vec<u8>>,
   288	    /// Set true when either task observes a permanent failure (WS
   289	    /// close, IO error, peer disconnect) OR caller invokes
   290	    /// [`close`](Self::close). Both `send` and `try_recv` honor this
   291	    /// flag per the `Transport` trait drain-before-close contract.
   292	    closed: Arc<AtomicBool>,
   293	    /// **V2 V3 step 4 audit closure (Opus M1, 2026-05-21):** stash
   294	    /// the most recent task-observed runtime error so callers can
   295	    /// distinguish "peer reset" from "auth rejected" from "capacity
   296	    /// exceeded" etc. Populated by the writer task on `ws_sink.send`
   297	    /// error and the reader task on stream `Err`. Stays `None` for
   298	    /// clean shutdowns (caller `close()`, Drop, or graceful Close
   299	    /// frame from peer).
   300	    last_error: Arc<Mutex<Option<WebSocketError>>>,
   301	    /// **Phase 5.5 V2 V4 V1 step 1 (2026-05-21) — Tier K1 ack channel.**
   302	    /// Incremented by [`Transport::send`] on Ok return. Total bytes
   303	    /// queued lifetime (monotonic, never resets). Compared against
   304	    /// [`Self::progress.0`] in [`Transport::flush_pending`] to detect
   305	    /// when the writer task has caught up.
   306	    queued_count: Arc<AtomicU64>,
   307	    /// **Phase 5.5 V2 V4 V1 step 1 (2026-05-21) — Tier K1 ack channel.**
   308	    /// `(counter, condvar)` pair. Counter is incremented by the writer
   309	    /// task AFTER each successful `ws_sink.send`. Condvar is notified
   310	    /// on each counter increment AND on `closed`-flag transition (so
   311	    /// `flush_pending` callers waiting on the Condvar wake up and
   312	    /// observe the closed state). Sync primitives (not tokio) because
   313	    /// `flush_pending` is called from sync caller code and needs to
   314	    /// block synchronously without a tokio runtime context.
   315	    progress: Arc<(Mutex<u64>, Condvar)>,
   316	    /// Background tokio task that drains `outbound_rx` and writes
   317	    /// `Message::Binary` frames to the WebSocket sink. Aborted on
   318	    /// `Drop`.
   319	    writer_task: JoinHandle<()>,
   320	    /// Background tokio task that polls the WebSocket stream and
   321	    /// pushes binary payloads into `inbound_tx`. Aborted on `Drop`.
   322	    reader_task: JoinHandle<()>,
   323	}
   324	
   325	impl std::fmt::Debug for WebSocketTransport {
   326	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
   327	        // **V2 V4 V1 step 4 (Tier K6, 2026-05-21):** surface
   328	        // last_error presence in Debug output. When a transport is
   329	        // closed and both tasks have exited, knowing whether the
   330	        // error slot is populated matters more than knowing the
   331	        // booleans alone — it distinguishes "clean caller-close"
   332	        // (last_error=None) from "task observed a runtime failure"
   333	        // (last_error=Some). Per V2 V3 step 5 megaudit Opus-B L2.
   334	        f.debug_struct("WebSocketTransport")
   335	            .field("closed", &self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
   336	            .field("writer_finished", &self.writer_task.is_finished())
   337	            .field("reader_finished", &self.reader_task.is_finished())
   338	            .field("last_error_present", &self.last_error().is_some())
   339	            .finish()
   340	    }
   341	}

   343	impl WebSocketTransport {
   344	    /// Connect to a WebSocket server at `url` (e.g. `ws://host:port/path`).
   345	    ///
   346	    /// Must be called from within a tokio runtime context (the two
   347	    /// background tasks are spawned via `tokio::spawn`). The typical
   348	    /// pattern from sync code is `runtime.block_on(connect(...))`.
   349	    ///
   350	    /// On success, returns a fully-wired transport: send/recv channels
   351	    /// connected, background tasks running. On failure, returns one
   352	    /// of the [`WebSocketError`] variants with the underlying cause.
   353	    pub async fn connect(url: &str) -> Result<Self, WebSocketError> {
   354	        // tokio-tungstenite::connect_async handles URL parse + TCP
   355	        // connect + WS handshake in one call. Distinguish the failure
   356	        // modes via the returned error string match — opaque to keep
   357	        // tungstenite types out of our public API.
   358	        let (ws_stream, _response) = tokio_tungstenite::connect_async(url).await.map_err(|e| {
   359	            let msg = e.to_string();
   360	            // Coarse classification — tungstenite::Error doesn't have a
   361	            // clean discriminant for "URL parse" vs "TCP connect" vs
   362	            // "handshake". Use the error type to route.
   363	            match e {
   364	                tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::Error::Url(_) => WebSocketError::InvalidUrl(msg),
   365	                tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::Error::Io(_) => WebSocketError::ConnectFailed(msg),
   366	                tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::Error::Http(_)
   367	                | tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::Error::HttpFormat(_) => {
   368	                    WebSocketError::HandshakeFailed(msg)
   369	                }
   370	                _ => WebSocketError::HandshakeFailed(msg),
   371	            }
   372	        })?;
   373	
   374	        let (mut ws_sink, mut ws_stream) = ws_stream.split();
   375	
   376	        let (outbound_tx, mut outbound_rx) = mpsc::unbounded_channel::<Vec<u8>>();
   377	        let (inbound_tx, inbound_rx) = mpsc::unbounded_channel::<Vec<u8>>();
   378	
   379	        let closed = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
   380	        let closed_writer = Arc::clone(&closed);
   381	        let closed_reader = Arc::clone(&closed);
   382	        let last_error = Arc::new(Mutex::new(None::<WebSocketError>));
   383	        let last_error_writer = Arc::clone(&last_error);
   384	        let last_error_reader = Arc::clone(&last_error);
   385	
   386	        // **Phase 5.5 V2 V4 V1 step 1 (2026-05-21) — Tier K1 ack channel.**
   387	        // Track writer-task progress for `Transport::flush_pending`.
   388	        // `queued_count` is incremented by `send()` after a successful
   389	        // mpsc enqueue. `progress.0` is the counter of bytes
   390	        // successfully flushed to the WebSocket sink, incremented by
   391	        // the writer task. `progress.1` (Condvar) is notified after
   392	        // each progress increment AND on closed-flag transitions, so
   393	        // `flush_pending` blocked in `wait_timeout` can wake and
   394	        // observe the new state.
   395	        let queued_count = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
   396	        let progress = Arc::new((Mutex::new(0u64), Condvar::new()));
   397	        let progress_writer = Arc::clone(&progress);
   398	        let progress_reader = Arc::clone(&progress);
   399	
   400	        // Writer task: drains outbound mpsc, writes Binary frames to
   401	        // the WS sink. Exits on outbound_rx close (caller dropped
   402	        // outbound_tx, which happens when WebSocketTransport drops)
   403	        // OR on sink error.
   404	        //
   405	        // **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Opus-B M2, 2026-05-21):**
   406	        // wrap the body in a TaskExitGuard so panic-unwinding
   407	        // sets `closed = true` + records a Panic error. Without
   408	        // this, a panic in `ws_sink.send`/`bytes.into()` leaves the
   409	        // transport in `closed=false` state with the writer task
   410	        // gone — callers send-loop forever returning Ok-but-discarded
   411	        // bytes.
   412	        let writer_task = tokio::spawn(async move {
   413	            let _guard = TaskExitGuard::new(
   414	                "writer",
   415	                Arc::clone(&closed_writer),
   416	                Arc::clone(&last_error_writer),
   417	                Arc::clone(&progress_writer),
   418	            );
   419	            while let Some(bytes) = outbound_rx.recv().await {
   420	                if let Err(e) = ws_sink.send(Message::Binary(bytes.into())).await {
   421	                    // V2 V3 step 4 audit closure (Opus M1): stash the
   422	                    // tungstenite error string so callers can read it
   423	                    // via last_error() after seeing TransportError::Closed.
   424	                    record_runtime_error(&last_error_writer, e.to_string());
   425	                    closed_writer.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   426	                    // V2 V4 V1 step 1: wake any flush_pending waiters
   427	                    // so they observe the now-set closed flag.
   428	                    progress_writer.1.notify_all();
   429	                    _guard.mark_clean_exit();
   430	                    return;
   430	                    return;
   431	                }
   432	                // V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1): writer task successfully
   433	                // wrote one byte blob to the WS sink. Advance the
   434	                // progress counter + notify any flush_pending waiters.
   435	                // **Step 1 audit closure (Opus L1):** poisoned-mutex
   436	                // handling — recover via PoisonError::into_inner()
   437	                // so a prior panic doesn't permanently freeze the
   438	                // counter at a stale value. Symmetric with
   439	                // last_error mutex handling.
   440	                let mut counter = match progress_writer.0.lock() {
   441	                    Ok(g) => g,
   442	                    Err(poisoned) => poisoned.into_inner(),
   443	                };
   444	                *counter += 1;
   445	                progress_writer.1.notify_all();
   446	            }
   447	            // outbound_rx closed (sender dropped) — clean shutdown.
   448	            // Attempt a graceful WS close frame; ignore errors (peer
   449	            // may already be gone). NOTE: under Drop, abort() runs
   450	            // before outbound_tx drops in field-decl order, so this
   451	            // arm is unreachable from Drop — see M2 closure note on
   452	            // the Drop impl. Reachable from a future "soft close" API
   453	            // that detaches outbound_tx explicitly.
   454	            let _ = ws_sink.close().await;
   455	            // V2 V4 V1 step 1: wake any flush_pending waiters on
   456	            // clean exit too (graceful "soft close" path).
   457	            progress_writer.1.notify_all();
   458	            _guard.mark_clean_exit();
   459	        });
   460	
   461	        // Reader task: polls WS stream; pushes binary payloads into
   462	        // inbound mpsc. Exits on stream end, error, or Close frame.
   463	        //
   464	        // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 audit closure (Codex L1 / Opus M1):** every
   465	        // closed-flag transition from the reader task now also calls
   466	        // `progress.1.notify_all()` so flush_pending waiters wake up
   467	        // immediately, not after a 100ms timeout. The TaskExitGuard
   468	        // also notifies on panic path via its Drop impl.
   469	        let reader_task = tokio::spawn(async move {
   470	            let _guard = TaskExitGuard::new(
   471	                "reader",
   472	                Arc::clone(&closed_reader),
   473	                Arc::clone(&last_error_reader),
   474	                Arc::clone(&progress_reader),
   475	            );
   476	            while let Some(msg_result) = ws_stream.next().await {
   477	                match msg_result {
   478	                    Ok(Message::Binary(bytes)) => {
   479	                        if inbound_tx.send(bytes.to_vec()).is_err() {
   480	                            // Receiver dropped (WebSocketTransport
   481	                            // dropped) — exit cleanly. Set closed
   482	                            // for state-machine symmetry (Opus-B L1).
   483	                            closed_reader.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   484	                            progress_reader.1.notify_all();
   485	                            _guard.mark_clean_exit();
   486	                            return;
   487	                        }
   488	                    }
   489	                    Ok(Message::Close(frame)) => {
   490	                        // **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Opus-B M4
   491	                        // + Codex L2, 2026-05-21):** capture the
   492	                        // close-frame code+reason if present. Empty
   493	                        // / missing CloseFrame stays last_error=None
   494	                        // for graceful close; populated CloseFrame
   495	                        // surfaces the application-level signal
   496	                        // (e.g., "session expired, please reauth").
   497	                        if let Some(cf) = frame {
   498	                            if !cf.reason.is_empty() || u16::from(cf.code) != 1000 {
   499	                                record_runtime_error(
   500	                                    &last_error_reader,
   501	                                    format!(
   502	                                        "peer close frame: code={}, reason={}",
   503	                                        u16::from(cf.code),
   504	                                        cf.reason
   505	                                    ),
   506	                                );
   507	                            }
   508	                        }
   509	                        closed_reader.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   510	                        progress_reader.1.notify_all();
   511	                        _guard.mark_clean_exit();
   512	                        return;
   513	                    }
   514	                    Ok(
   515	                        Message::Text(_) | Message::Ping(_) | Message::Pong(_) | Message::Frame(_),
   516	                    ) => {
   517	                        // Non-binary frames dropped per protocol
   518	                        // contract (see module-level V1 limits).
   519	                    }
   520	                    Err(e) => {
   521	                        // V2 V3 step 4 audit closure (Opus M1): stash
   522	                        // the tungstenite error so callers can
   523	                        // distinguish runtime causes via last_error().
   524	                        record_runtime_error(&last_error_reader, e.to_string());
   525	                        closed_reader.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   526	                        progress_reader.1.notify_all();
   527	                        _guard.mark_clean_exit();
   528	                        return;
   529	                    }
   530	                }
   531	            }
   532	            // **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Codex L2 + Opus-B M4,
   533	            // 2026-05-21):** stream ended without a Close frame.
   534	            // Distinguishable from clean caller-close (last_error
   535	            // stays None) and from explicit Close frame (last_error
   536	            // populated above if frame had reason or non-1000 code).
   537	            record_runtime_error(
   538	                &last_error_reader,
   539	                "peer stream ended without close frame".to_string(),
   540	            );
   541	            closed_reader.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   542	            progress_reader.1.notify_all();
   543	            _guard.mark_clean_exit();
   544	        });
   545	
   546	        Ok(Self {
   547	            outbound_tx,
   548	            inbound_rx,
   549	            closed,
   550	            last_error,
   551	            queued_count,
   552	            progress,
   553	            writer_task,
   554	            reader_task,
   555	        })
   556	    }
   557	
   558	    /// True if this transport has been closed — either explicitly via
   559	    /// [`close`](Self::close), via Drop, or by either background task
   560	    /// observing a permanent failure (peer disconnect, WS Close frame,
   561	    /// IO error).
   562	    pub fn is_closed(&self) -> bool {
   563	        self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
   564	    }
   565	
   566	    /// **V2 V3 step 4 audit closure (Opus M1, 2026-05-21):** read the
   567	    /// most recent task-observed runtime error, if any. Returns `None`
   568	    /// for clean shutdowns (caller [`close`](Self::close), Drop, or
   569	    /// graceful Close frame from peer); returns `Some(RuntimeError(_))`
   570	    /// when the writer's `ws_sink.send` or the reader's `ws_stream.next`
   571	    /// surfaced an error before exiting.
   572	    ///
   573	    /// Read AFTER observing [`TransportError::Closed`] from
   574	    /// [`Transport::send`] or [`Transport::try_recv`] to distinguish
   575	    /// "peer reset" vs "auth rejected" vs "capacity exceeded" etc.
   576	    /// IDE consumers driving reconnect handshakes use this to choose
   577	    /// the right user-facing message and backoff strategy.
   578	    ///
   579	    /// Returns a clone (cheap — `WebSocketError` is small + `Clone`).
   580	    ///
   581	    /// **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Opus-B M3, 2026-05-21):**
   582	    /// poisoned mutex no longer silently returns `None`. Recovers
   583	    /// the inner via `PoisonError::into_inner()` so the slot's
   584	    /// most-recent contents stay readable across the poison boundary.
   585	    pub fn last_error(&self) -> Option<WebSocketError> {
   586	        match self.last_error.lock() {
   587	            Ok(guard) => guard.clone(),
   588	            Err(poisoned) => poisoned.into_inner().clone(),
   589	        }
   590	    }
   591	
   592	    /// Explicitly mark this transport closed. Subsequent
   593	    /// [`Transport::send`] calls return `Err(Closed)`; subsequent
   594	    /// [`Transport::try_recv`] calls drain the inbound queue first,
   595	    /// then return `Err(Closed)` (per trait contract).
   596	    ///
   597	    /// Does NOT abort the background tasks — only Drop does that. If
   598	    /// the caller wants the tasks gone, drop the transport.
   599	    ///
   600	    /// **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1):** also notifies the
   601	    /// flush_pending Condvar so any concurrent `flush_pending` waiter
   602	    /// wakes up and observes the new closed state.
   603	    pub fn close(&self) {
   604	        self.closed.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   605	        self.progress.1.notify_all();
   606	    }
   607	}

   609	impl Drop for WebSocketTransport {
   610	    fn drop(&mut self) {
   611	        // **V2 V3 step 4 audit closure (Opus M2, 2026-05-21):** the
   612	        // sole shutdown path under current design is `abort()` on both
   613	        // task handles. The graceful `outbound_rx.recv() -> None ->
   614	        // ws_sink.close()` branch in the writer task is UNREACHABLE
   615	        // FROM DROP because `Drop::drop` runs before the struct's
   616	        // fields drop (Rust drop order: body first, then fields in
   617	        // decl order). So `outbound_tx` is still alive when we call
   618	        // `writer_task.abort()`. The graceful arm only fires if a
   619	        // future "soft close" API explicitly detaches `outbound_tx`
   620	        // before drop — not part of the current MVP.
   621	        //
   622	        // `closed = true` ordering: set first so any concurrent
   623	        // sync `send`/`try_recv` observes Closed via the flag check
   624	        // before the task abort propagates.
   625	        //
   626	        // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1):** also notify the
   627	        // flush_pending Condvar — a caller awaiting a long-running
   628	        // flush would otherwise wait until the next wait_timeout
   629	        // tick to observe the closed flag. (Unreachable in practice
   630	        // because Drop is called on a unique `&mut self` so no
   631	        // concurrent flush_pending can be in flight, but kept for
   632	        // safety + future shared-reference APIs.)
   633	        self.closed.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   634	        self.progress.1.notify_all();
   635	        self.writer_task.abort();
   636	        self.reader_task.abort();
   637	    }
   638	}

   641	    fn send(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
   642	        // **LOAD-BEARING** (V2 V3 step 4 audit closure, Opus M4): this
   643	        // closed-flag check MUST precede `outbound_tx.send`. The
   644	        // `collab_session_websocket_send_after_close_surfaces_closed`
   645	        // integration test depends on observing `Closed` here (the
   646	        // reader task sets `closed = true` on peer disconnect; the
   647	        // writer task may still be parked on `outbound_rx.recv` and
   648	        // hasn't yet seen the broken sink). If a future refactor
   649	        // reorders this check (e.g., to enable an outbox-queuing-
   650	        // while-closed feature), that test will flake.
   651	        if self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
   652	            return Err(TransportError::Closed);
   653	        }
   654	        // UnboundedSender::send returns Err iff the receiver dropped.
   655	        // The receiver lives in the writer task; if it dropped, the
   656	        // task exited (panic, abort, or graceful). Treat as Closed.
   657	        self.outbound_tx
   658	            .send(bytes.to_vec())
   659	            .map_err(|_| TransportError::Closed)?;
   660	        // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (2026-05-21) — Tier K1 ack channel.**
   661	        // Bump the queued-count counter AFTER successful mpsc enqueue.
   662	        // flush_pending() reads this as the target the writer task
   663	        // must catch up to.
   664	        self.queued_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
   665	        Ok(())
   666	    }

   670	        // (transport.rs:112-115): "Closed only when channel

   709	    /// **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (2026-05-21) — Tier K1 ack channel.**
   710	    /// Block until every byte blob previously queued via `send` has
   711	    /// been written to the WebSocket sink. Closes the V2 V3 step 5
   712	    /// megaudit's convergent finding (queued-vs-acked semantics).
   713	    ///
   714	    /// Mechanism: reads `queued_count` as the target; locks the
   715	    /// `progress.0` counter and uses `Condvar::wait_timeout` to wake
   716	    /// every 100ms (so closed-flag transitions are observed promptly).
   717	    /// The writer task increments `progress.0` + `notify_all` after
   718	    /// each successful `ws_sink.send`, AND `notify_all` on closed-
   719	    /// flag transitions.
   720	    ///
   721	    /// # Errors
   722	    /// - `TransportError::Closed` if the transport was already closed
   723	    ///   on entry, OR if the writer task sets closed mid-wait (e.g.,
   724	    ///   ws_sink.send failed).
   725	    /// - `TransportError::Io` if the progress mutex is poisoned by a
   726	    ///   panicked writer task. The poisoned-mutex recovery via
   727	    ///   `PoisonError::into_inner()` is intentionally NOT used here:
   728	    ///   if the writer panicked mid-counter-increment, the counter
   729	    ///   may be in an inconsistent state (e.g., notify_all happened
   730	    ///   before counter increment); reading + retrying could
   731	    ///   busy-loop forever. Surface as Io and let the caller
   732	    ///   recover via reconnect.
   733	    fn flush_pending(&mut self) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
   734	        // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 audit closure (Codex M1, 2026-05-21):**
   735	        // honor the documented contract — if the transport is closed
   736	        // on entry, return Err(Closed) immediately, regardless of
   737	        // whether the local progress counter has already caught up.
   738	        // The prior impl returned Ok in this case, contradicting the
   739	        // docstring + the closed-on-entry test which now accepts
   740	        // both Ok and Err. After this closure, the contract is "Err
   741	        // if closed at any point — entry or mid-wait".
   742	        if self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
   743	            return Err(TransportError::Closed);
   744	        }
   745	        let target = self.queued_count.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
   746	        let (counter_lock, cv) = &*self.progress;
   747	        let mut counter = counter_lock
   748	            .lock()
   749	            .map_err(|e| TransportError::Io(format!("flush_pending lock poisoned: {e}")))?;
   750	        while *counter < target {
   751	            if self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
   752	                return Err(TransportError::Closed);
   753	            }
   754	            let (new_counter, _timeout_result) = cv
   755	                .wait_timeout(counter, Duration::from_millis(100))
   756	                .map_err(|e| TransportError::Io(format!("flush_pending wait poisoned: {e}")))?;
   757	            counter = new_counter;
   758	        }
   759	        Ok(())
   760	    }
   761	}

     4	//! All tests run on a `current_thread` tokio runtime built per-test
     5	//! so they're independently schedulable; `--test-threads=1` is fine

    37	/// Build a single-threaded tokio runtime for one test. Each test owns
    38	/// its runtime so panics + abort() cleanups can't leak across tests.
    39	fn runtime() -> tokio::runtime::Runtime {
    40	    tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
    41	        .enable_all()
    42	        .build()
    43	        .expect("build tokio runtime")

    46	/// **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1):** multi-thread runtime for tests that
    47	/// call sync `flush_pending()`. The single-threaded runtime above
    48	/// would deadlock because flush_pending blocks the worker thread via
    49	/// `Condvar::wait_timeout`, preventing the writer/reader tokio tasks
    50	/// from making progress. Multi-thread runtime gives the tokio tasks
    51	/// their own workers. This matches the documented async-context
    52	/// caveat in `Transport::flush_pending` — real IDE consumers either
    53	/// run on a multi-thread runtime OR wrap the call in
    54	/// `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`.
    55	fn multi_thread_runtime() -> tokio::runtime::Runtime {
    56	    tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread()
    57	        .worker_threads(2)
    58	        .enable_all()
    59	        .build()
    60	        .expect("build multi-thread tokio runtime")
    61	}

    63	/// Poll `try_recv` with short sleeps for up to `max_iters * 10ms`
    64	/// looking for a binary blob. Async background tasks need a chance
    65	/// to deliver bytes; tests block on this helper.

   683	    // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1):** pin the blocking-then-Ok semantic.

   685	    // returns Ok AFTER the writer task has caught up (i.e., the echo
   686	    // server has reflected the blobs back).

   691	            .await
   692	            .expect("handshake");

   695	            ws.send(&[i, i + 1, i + 2]).expect("send");
   696	        }
   697	
   698	        // flush_pending should block until all 5 sends are flushed.
   699	        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
   700	        let result = ws.flush_pending();
   701	        let elapsed = start.elapsed();
   702	
   703	        assert!(
   704	            result.is_ok(),
   705	            "flush_pending after 5 sends MUST return Ok once writer drains, got {result:?}"
   706	        );
   707	        // Some blocking time is expected (mpsc + ws_sink + tokio
   708	        // scheduling). Upper bound is generous for slow CI.
   709	        assert!(
   710	            elapsed < Duration::from_secs(2),
   711	            "flush_pending blocked unreasonably long: {elapsed:?}"
   712	        );
   713	
   714	        // Echo verification: each blob should have been sent over
   715	        // the wire (and echoed back).
   716	        let mut received = 0;
   717	        for _ in 0..30 {
   718	            match ws.try_recv() {
   719	                Ok(Some(_)) => received += 1,
   720	                Ok(None) => tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await,
   721	                Err(_) => break,
   722	            }
   723	            if received >= 5 {
   724	                break;
   725	            }
   726	        }
   727	        assert_eq!(
   728	            received, 5,
   729	            "all 5 blobs MUST have been flushed (and echoed back), got {received}"
   730	        );
   731	    });
   732	}

   735	fn flush_pending_after_close_returns_closed() {
   736	    // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1):** closed-state fast-path. If the
   737	    // transport is already closed on entry, flush_pending returns
   738	    // Err(Closed) immediately — regardless of whether the local
   739	    // progress counter has caught up.
   740	    //
   741	    // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 audit closure (Codex M1, 2026-05-21):** prior
   742	    // version of this test accepted EITHER Ok OR Err(Closed) because
   743	    // the impl returned Ok if `counter >= target` on entry, even when
   744	    // closed. The audit caught the docstring-vs-impl divergence. The
   745	    // closure inverted the impl to check `closed` BEFORE the
   746	    // counter-vs-target check, so closed-on-entry now uniformly
   747	    // returns Err(Closed) per the documented contract.
   748	    let rt = multi_thread_runtime();
   749	    rt.block_on(async {
   750	        let server = EchoServer::start().await;
   751	        let mut ws = WebSocketTransport::connect(&server.url())
   752	            .await
   753	            .expect("handshake");
   754	
   755	        // Queue a few sends, close the transport explicitly, then
   756	        // flush_pending.
   757	        ws.send(b"a").expect("send");
   758	        ws.send(b"b").expect("send");
   759	        ws.close();
   760	
   761	        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
   762	        let result = ws.flush_pending();
   763	        let elapsed = start.elapsed();
   764	
   765	        assert!(
   766	            matches!(result, Err(TransportError::Closed)),
   767	            "flush_pending after explicit close MUST return Err(Closed), got {result:?}"
   768	        );
   769	        assert!(
   770	            elapsed < Duration::from_millis(50),
   771	            "closed-on-entry flush_pending MUST be near-instant (skip the wait loop), got {elapsed:?}"
   772	        );
   773	    });
   774	}

   776	#[test]
   777	fn flush_pending_returns_closed_if_server_drops_mid_flush() {
   778	    // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1):** pin the "writer fails mid-flush"
   779	    // path. Server is dropped while flush_pending is parked on the
   780	    // Condvar. Reader task sees disconnect → sets closed → notifies
   781	    // Condvar (via Drop on EchoServer aborting per-conn tasks → TCP
   782	    // socket dies → ws_stream errors → reader sets closed). The
   783	    // writer task notify_all on closed-flag transition wakes up
   784	    // flush_pending which observes the closed flag and returns
   785	    // Err(Closed).
   786	    let rt = multi_thread_runtime();
   787	    rt.block_on(async {
   788	        let server = EchoServer::start().await;
   789	        let mut ws = WebSocketTransport::connect(&server.url())
   790	            .await
   791	            .expect("handshake");
   792	
   793	        // Queue some sends.
   794	        ws.send(b"in-flight-1").expect("send");
   795	        ws.send(b"in-flight-2").expect("send");
   796	
   797	        // Drop the server — TCP socket dies on per-conn abort.
   798	        drop(server);
   799	
   800	        // flush_pending should eventually observe the closed state and
   801	        // return Err. Acceptable: also returns Ok if the writer
   802	        // happened to send both blobs before the TCP teardown was
   803	        // observed.
   804	        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
   805	        let result = ws.flush_pending();
   806	        let elapsed = start.elapsed();
   807	
   808	        match result {
   809	            Ok(()) | Err(TransportError::Closed) => {}
   810	            other => panic!("expected Ok or Err(Closed), got {other:?}"),
   811	        }
   812	        // Should not hang. The Condvar wait_timeout is 100ms; the
   813	        // closed flag should be observed within a few iterations.
   814	        assert!(
   815	            elapsed < Duration::from_secs(3),
   816	            "flush_pending hung post-server-drop: {elapsed:?}"
   817	        );
   818	    });
   819	}

    10	/// A mutual exclusion primitive useful for protecting shared data
    11	///
    12	/// This mutex will block threads waiting for the lock to become available. The
    13	/// mutex can be statically initialized or created by the `new`
    14	/// constructor. Each mutex has a type parameter which represents the data that
    15	/// it is protecting. The data can only be accessed through the RAII guards
    16	/// returned from `lock` and `try_lock`, which guarantees that the data is only
    17	/// ever accessed when the mutex is locked.
    18	///
    19	/// # Fairness
    20	///
    21	/// A typical unfair lock can often end up in a situation where a single thread
    22	/// quickly acquires and releases the same mutex in succession, which can starve
    23	/// other threads waiting to acquire the mutex. While this improves throughput
    24	/// because it doesn't force a context switch when a thread tries to re-acquire
    25	/// a mutex it has just released, this can starve other threads.
    26	///
    27	/// This mutex uses [eventual fairness](https://trac.webkit.org/changeset/203350)
    28	/// to ensure that the lock will be fair on average without sacrificing
    29	/// throughput. This is done by forcing a fair unlock on average every 0.5ms,
    30	/// which will force the lock to go to the next thread waiting for the mutex.
    31	///
    32	/// Additionally, any critical section longer than 1ms will always use a fair
    33	/// unlock, which has a negligible impact on throughput considering the length
    34	/// of the critical section.
    35	///
    36	/// You can also force a fair unlock by calling `MutexGuard::unlock_fair` when
    37	/// unlocking a mutex instead of simply dropping the `MutexGuard`.
    38	///
    39	/// # Differences from the standard library `Mutex`
    40	///
    41	/// - No poisoning, the lock is released normally on panic.
    42	/// - Only requires 1 byte of space, whereas the standard library boxes the
    43	///   `Mutex` due to platform limitations.
    44	/// - Can be statically constructed.
    45	/// - Does not require any drop glue when dropped.
    46	/// - Inline fast path for the uncontended case.
    47	/// - Efficient handling of micro-contention using adaptive spinning.
    48	/// - Allows raw locking & unlocking without a guard.
    49	/// - Supports eventual fairness so that the mutex is fair on average.
    50	/// - Optionally allows making the mutex fair by calling `MutexGuard::unlock_fair`.
    51	///
    52	/// # Examples
    53	///
    54	/// ```
    55	/// use parking_lot::Mutex;
    56	/// use std::sync::{Arc, mpsc::channel};
    57	/// use std::thread;
    58	///

    88	/// Creates a new mutex in an unlocked state ready for use.
    89	///

   130	/// A mutual exclusion primitive useful for protecting shared data
   131	///
   132	/// This mutex will block threads waiting for the lock to become available. The
   133	/// mutex can also be statically initialized or created via a `new`
   134	/// constructor. Each mutex has a type parameter which represents the data that
   135	/// it is protecting. The data can only be accessed through the RAII guards
   136	/// returned from `lock` and `try_lock`, which guarantees that the data is only
   137	/// ever accessed when the mutex is locked.
   138	pub struct Mutex<R, T: ?Sized> {
   139	    raw: R,
   140	    data: UnsafeCell<T>,
   141	}

   144	unsafe impl<R: RawMutex + Sync, T: ?Sized + Send> Sync for Mutex<R, T> {}

   146	impl<R: RawMutex, T> Mutex<R, T> {
   147	    /// Creates a new mutex in an unlocked state ready for use.
   148	    #[inline]
   149	    pub const fn new(val: T) -> Mutex<R, T> {
   150	        Mutex {
   151	            raw: R::INIT,
   152	            data: UnsafeCell::new(val),
   153	        }

The runtime side checks out: napi-rs 3.9.0 builds a `new_multi_thread().enable_all()` runtime, and Tokio 1.50.0 defaults `max_blocking_threads` to 512. The main weakness I’m seeing is in the tests: the Loopback-based “interleaving” cases don’t force a real pending flush or lock contention, so they are smoke tests rather than proof of the concurrency property.

PASS-WITH-FINDINGS

**Findings**

LOW: stale Send/Sync safety docs in [lib.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-bindings-node/src/lib.rs:70) and [lib.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-bindings-node/src/lib.rs:1091).  
What: module docs and the old commented `!Sync` probe still say the binding `CollabSession` is `Send + !Sync`, contradicting the V2.4 `Arc<Mutex<...>>` shape and positive `assert_sync::<CollabSession>()`.  
Why: not runtime-unsound, but it undermines the Rule 4 safety narrative.  
Closure: replace the old V1/V2.3 block with the V2.4 `Send + Sync` explanation, or delete the obsolete `!Sync` probe entirely.

LOW: V2.4 “soundness” tests are smoke tests, not strong contention tests, in [quantbook-roundtrip.test.ts](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab/extensions/quantlab/test/quantbook-roundtrip.test.ts:1211) and [quantbook-roundtrip.test.ts](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab/extensions/quantlab/test/quantbook-roundtrip.test.ts:1227).  
What: `Promise.all` creates overlapping native promises, but the Loopback transport’s `flush_pending` is the default immediate `Ok(())`, so no real pending wait or mutex contention is forced.  
Why: the tests would catch gross crashes/hangs, but they do not prove the V2.3 UB hazard is gone. The proof is structural in Rust (`&self` + mutex + compile checks).  
Closure: add a test-only slow/blocking transport or delayed WebSocket fixture that holds `flushPendingToTransport` long enough to prove same-session calls serialize and sync calls block/release in order.

LOW: V2.4 loader skew check is not directly pinned by a stale V2.3 fixture. The check exists in [loader.ts](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab/extensions/quantlab/src/quantbook/loader.ts:265), but the visible stale-binary tests stop at V2.1/V2.2 shape.  
Why: boundary behavior could regress without a focused test failing.  
Closure: add a fake V2.3-shaped module with `Transport.websocketConnect` and all V2.2 methods, but no `CollabSession.prototype.flushPendingToTransport`, and assert the V2.4 missing-export message.

OBS: same-session concurrent `flushPendingToTransport` calls are safe but can consume multiple Tokio blocking threads while losers wait on the mutex. This does not starve the worker pool; Tokio’s default blocking cap is 512, then tasks queue. For pathological duplicate calls or a permanently stuck transport, consider coalescing in-flight flushes or adding timeout/cancel semantics.

**Verified**

All `CollabSession` binding methods that touch `self.inner` now lock internally; no `CollabSession` napi method still takes `&mut self`. The async method only clones the `Arc` before `.await`; the mutex guard is created inside `spawn_blocking`, so no guard is held across await.

`napi-rs` accepts async `&self` without `unsafe`: its codegen rejects async `&mut self` unless unsafe, while `&self` becomes a shared leaked reference. The generated future is `Send`, so the new `CollabSession: Sync` assertion is load-bearing and correct.

`spawn_blocking` closure is sound for HIGH-2: napi-rs 3.9.0 creates a multi-thread Tokio runtime, and Tokio 1.50.0 defaults `max_blocking_threads` to 512. `CoreCollabSession::flush_pending_to_transport` itself does not spawn more Tokio work; it delegates to the transport’s blocking `flush_pending`.

Validation: `/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/bin/cargo check -p ql-bindings-node` passed.
